newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Sihanouk concerned at political situation.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Sihanouk concerned at political situation.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk said on Friday he was concerned about the country's political situation, and officials said security forces would stay neutral amid tension between the two rival prime ministers.

"I have a great and deep concern about the political situation, divisive arguments and threats between some people," the 74-year-old Sihanouk said in a letter from Beijing, where he is recovering from an eye operation.

The king, in a statement released by his palace, said he could not intervene to try to solve the current political crisis and avert the threat of fighting between the royalist FUNCINPEC party and the Cambodian People's Party (CPP).

FUNCINPEC and the CPP formed an uneasy coalition government after U.N.-run 1993 polls. Ties between co-Premiers Hun Sen of the CPP and Prince Norodom Ranariddh of FUNCINPEC have been strained for some time. "I only pray and hold my hands up to Buddha and the former kings and queens, 'Please rescue our nation to avoid misery, disaster and return to stability, peace, unity, solidarity and brotherhood again'", he said.
The king, who reigns but does not rule, stoked the political rift within the government by saying earlier this year he was unhappy on the throne and wanted to abdicate.

His message of concern came after eight top officials, four from each party, agreed at a meeting that the police and armed forces should remain neutral and avoid bloodshed in the war of words between the co-premiers.
Co-Interior Minister Sar Kheng, speaking after the meeting, said the order would be given to senior soldiers, police and civil servants from around the nation at a meeting on Tuesday.
"We hope and believe that after this meeting and the meeting on April 29, we can solve the situation in Cambodia, especially the political situation," he said.

Sar Kheng told reporters the four CPP and four FUNCINPEC officials at Friday's meeting had been instructed by Hun Sen and Ranariddh to meet in a bid to ease political tension and curb the risk of violence between their rival armed forces.
"The eight of us fully agreed to completely avoid confrontation with weapons," Sar Kheng said after the meeting.
Tension between the two parties has soared since a deadly March 30 grenade attack on a demonstration led by opposition leaders and FUNCINPEC ally, Sam Rainsy.
Ties hit a low last week when Hun Sen said the CPP backed a challenge to Ranariddh's leadership of FUNCINPEC, from royalist dissidents. The news sparked rumours of an imminent coup.
